agents.note: SPRINT 66 (V0.29.20) -- US-494 (S1 splash handoff) DONE, 1/7. THE SHAPE OF THIS BUG IS THE LESSON: it took TWO defects that each look harmless alone. The wiring defect -- eclipse-boot-state.service constructs BootStateEmitter with only statesDir+hardCapSeconds, so obdProbeFn fell to its default `lambda: OBD_STARTING` -- and the coupling defect -- that tier GATED the splash handoff. Either one alone is survivable; together the tier never went terminal, progress capped at 2/3, healthy never went true, boot-state-poll.js never called window.close(), and splash-boot.service's OnSuccess=eclipse-dashboard.service never fired. After the 12s cap it degraded to the literal string 'eclipse-obd: not ready (starting)' and held there until reboot. MOST IMPORTANT CARRY-FORWARD: no test of computeBootState could ever have caught this, in any shape, because computeBootState was always CORRECT. The bug lived entirely in what main() failed to pass it. A pure function with 13 passing tests sat next to a two-line constructor call that made the whole subsystem useless. So I extracted buildEmitter() purely to make the production wiring assertable, and test_main_wiresTheCoreOnlyGate asserts on the emitter main() actually hands runForever. WHEN A DEFAULT ARGUMENT IS THE BUG, TEST THE CALLER. SECOND, and this is the same finding as last sprint's `unknown`-means-SAFE-SHUTDOWN-GUARD-IS-DOWN banner: the offending default was a LIE, not merely a wrong value. OBD_STARTING asserts checks are IN PROGRESS. No check was ever wired, so that claim could never become true. Added OBD_NOT_PROBED ('not-probed') as the honest default. Two sprints running, the real bug has been a missing READING rendered as a confident STATE -- I now treat `X or <plausible-default>` as a code smell on sight. THIRD: readiness was conflating two different facts -- 'is the Pi UI up' and 'is a car plugged in'. The Pi lives on a bench most of the time, so a vehicle-shaped readiness gate makes the dashboard structurally unreachable there. CORE_SERVICES_DEFAULT is now eclipse-states-http + eclipse-powerwatch + boot-progress-finalize + the dashboard assets; eclipse-obd is sampled and published in its own non-gating `obdTier` field. PAYLOAD SHAPE CHANGED -- whoever builds S3/US-496 or any vehicle-slice card must read this: `services` now holds ONLY systemctl states (it used to overwrite the eclipse-obd entry with a tier verdict); new fields are obdTier, coreServices and uiAssets. Grep-verified the only external consumer is boot-state-poll.js reading healthy/degraded/degradedReason/progress, so no JS needed touching. JUDGEMENT CALL for PM/Atlas: I made MISSING DASHBOARD ASSETS a degrade (holds the splash, reason 'dashboard assets not installed') rather than merely not-healthy -- handing off to a dashboard that was never installed IS the A-16 blank screen, so this turns a silent blank screen into a named message. A failed core unit outranks it in the one-line reason. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: did NOT gate on the Pi-local emitters despite design v5 S1 mentioning them, because they run under the orchestrator inside eclipse-obd.service -- gating on them smuggles the vehicle coupling back in through the side door. AC-1's narrower wording is the correct gate. GREEN: 172 passed/1 skipped in tests/pi/splash (22 in the rewritten boot-state module) + 100 in tests/deploy/test_deploy_pi.py and tests/pi/ops, ruff clean. HOST GAPS UNCHANGED from Sprint 64: make, black and mypy are all absent on this Windows box -- the story asks for 'Typecheck green', so PM must run mypy at integration time. ON-PI GATE OWED (AC-4, undischargeable from a dev box): bench-boot with NO car and watch the splash hand off; curl boot-state for healthy:true / obdTier:'not-probed' / uiAssets:'present'. Do the curl FIRST -- if uiAssets reads 'missing' the splash now holds with 'dashboard assets not installed', which is the honest report of a real stale-/opt condition (precisely what US-495 force-refreshes), NOT a regression of this story. Restarting eclipse-boot-state.service re-checks it without a reboot. Architecture DoD met in-sprint (Rule 10): specs/architecture.md F-103 section gained a 'Readiness contract' subsection; also corrected the unit-file header, which still described the old gate. Carried debt unchanged: TD-067, TD-068.
